summary: Round r1 (restricted network). (1) Post-graduation preferences: the EU replaced Regulation (EU) No 978/2012 with Regulation (EU) 2026/1395 (reported to apply from 1 January 2027), so Nepal's EBA exit and any GSP+ application will fall under the new text; UK DCTS moves LDC graduates from Comprehensive to Enhanced Preferences after a transition period, with Bhutan as precedent. Transition length, GSP+ vulnerability and convention criteria and the Nepal graduation date (reported as November 2026, with a UN CDP request to extend the preparatory period noted by 16A) must be read from primary texts. (2) Regulatory exposure: CBAM (definitive period from 2026), EUDR (delayed to end-2026), Forced Labour Regulation (applies later) and CSDDD as amended by Omnibus I (Directive (EU) 2026/470) were located; product-level mapping to Nepal's EU export basket requires customs/Comtrade data. No values retrieved; all empirical items pending.

findings.claim: Nepal's effective date of UN LDC graduation and whether the preparatory period is extended under the CDP crisis response process.
findings.note: Governs start of EU EBA and UK Comprehensive transition clocks; retrieve UNGA resolution and CDP 2026 decision (16A leads L47/L48).

findings.claim: EU: legal transition period and end date of EBA for Nepal under Regulation (EU) 2026/1395 (and transitional provisions from 978/2012), and resulting tariff treatment (standard GSP vs GSP+).
findings.note: Read graduation/transition articles and Annex I of 18C-L01; compare with 978/2012 (L02).

findings.claim: EU GSP+ eligibility for Nepal: vulnerability criteria (import-share and concentration tests), list of required conventions and Nepal's ratification/reporting status for each.
findings.note: Criteria from 18C-L01 annexes; ratification status from UN Treaty Collection and ILO NORMLEX (not yet leads).

findings.claim: Tariff differential for Nepal's main EU export lines (carpets, apparel, pashmina/textiles, tea, others) between EBA, GSP+, standard GSP and MFN.
findings.note: Annex III of 18C-L01, EU TARIC/Access2Markets; ITC study L18 for comparison.

findings.claim: UK: transition period and date Nepal moves from DCTS Comprehensive to Enhanced Preferences, eligibility under the vulnerability test, and rules-of-origin changes.
Nepal's exports to the EU and UK by HS product and their share of total exports (Nepal customs FY and Eurostat/HMRC calendar year).
findings.note: Required to weight preference losses and regulatory exposure; keep FY vs calendar year separate.

findings.claim: CBAM exposure: value of Nepal exports to the EU in CBAM Annex I CN codes.
findings.note: Map Annex I of 18C-L12 to Nepal's EU exports; expected to be small but must be measured, not assumed.

findings.claim: EUDR exposure: Nepal EU exports in EUDR commodity scope (e.g. coffee, wood products, leather) and application dates for large vs micro/small operators.
findings.note: 18C-L15; HS mapping from EUDR Annex I.

findings.claim: Forced Labour Regulation and CSDDD (as amended) pass-through to Nepali suppliers: application dates, company thresholds and sectors at elevated risk (e.g. carpets, garments, bricks in supply chains).
findings.note: 18C-L14, L16, L17; ILO/US DoL child and forced labour evidence for Nepal sectors (not yet leads).

findings.claim: Graduation-related preference changes are modelled as legal events with dated effect on applied tariffs, separate from regulatory (CBAM/EUDR/FLR/CSDDD) compliance costs, which are modelled as non-tariff trade costs.
Where search results report dates for EU/UK instruments, those dates are treated as unverified until the Official Journal / legislation.gov.uk text is retrieved.

assumptions.text: Preference-regime changes (tariffs) and regulatory compliance costs (non-tariff) are modelled separately.
Transition clocks start at the effective UN graduation date, which is itself pending (possible extension).
Eurostat/HMRC partner data (calendar year, importer-reported) and Nepal customs (FY, exporter-reported) will differ; both are kept.

challenges.text: EU EBA exit now falls under Regulation (EU) 2026/1395, not 978/2012; preference-loss estimates based on the old regulation's GSP+ criteria must be re-checked against the new text.
S08 LDC-graduation timing depends on the CDP extension request; EU and UK transition end dates move with it - do not hard-code a graduation year.
Add regulatory non-tariff measures (CBAM, EUDR, FLR, CSDDD) as an external variable or sub-variable of X12 with 18C as primary supplier; currently only tariff preferences are listed.
Escalation: if the new EU GSP changes GSP+ eligibility conditions for LDC graduates, the S08 conclusion on EU market access may change; flag for audit once the text is retrieved.

uncertainty: High. Legal texts were located but not downloaded; dates and rules come from search snippets and are unverified. Nepal's graduation date itself is uncertain because of the reported CDP extension request. Product-level exposure cannot be assessed until trade data are retrieved.

post_graduation_preferences.method: For EU and UK record: legal instrument, current Nepal tier, transition length and end date (conditional on graduation date), post-transition tier options with eligibility tests, and tariff differentials for Nepal's top export lines.

regulatory_exposure.method: Map each regulation's product scope (CN/HS codes) and application dates to Nepal's EU export basket by HS6; classify exposure as direct (goods in scope) or pass-through (buyer due diligence).
